## Intent
Hypothesis: per-particle component-wise NEON vectorization with 4× loop unrolling can approach the streaming ceiling despite branchy respawn.

## Cache saturation
The L1d spill (N≈963) lies below the smallest measured point (N=10000), so its effect is invisible. The L2 spill (N≈61680) falls between N=10000 and N=100000. At death_q=0.01, ns/p FALLS from 8.46 (N=10000) to 7.65 (N=100000) and continues to 7.246 (N=10000000) — overhead amortization dominates with no knee at the L2→DRAM spill. At death_q=0.1 the curve is FLAT at ~9.0 ns/p (8.991 to 8.913), and at q=0.25 and q=0.5 it is likewise FLAT (10.887 to 11.14, 13.3 to 13.61), confirming that death rate raises the floor without changing the N-shape. No cache-spill knee appears at any death rate.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 9.38 GB/s at N=10000000, death_q=0.01 — 31% of the 29.9 GB/s streaming ceiling. Bandwidth is FLAT across N at each death rate, confirming the algo is overhead-bound, not bandwidth-bound. As death rate rises, achieved bandwidth drops monotonically: 9.38 → 7.63 → 6.10 → 5.00 GB/s for q = 0.01, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5. The transition is driven entirely by death rate, not by N or cache spill. The branch_flush cycle bucket grows from 7.1% (q=0.01) to 37.4% (q=0.5), consuming the budget that would otherwise go to useful memory traffic.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized component-wise within a single particle, not across particles. The core update loads 4 floats with `ldr q1`, 2 more with `ldr d2`, rearranges via `ext.16b v3, v1, v2, #0xc`, then `fmul.4s v0, v3, v4` and `fadd.4s v0, v1, v0` for the 4-lane position update, stored back with `str q0`. A gather appears: `ld1.s {v2}[1], [x8]` loads a single indexed float into lane 1, followed by `fmul.2s`/`fadd.2s` on the 2-lane velocity. The LP1-unroll processes 4 particles per iteration (stride 0x110 = 272 = 4×68 bytes), each with its own scalar `fcmp`/`b.ge` death check and `bl _layouts.ML01.data.Data.spawn` call. The render loop uses `ldrb`/`strb` byte-granular pixel stores with `csel` clamping. Each respawn path contains `udiv`/`msub` for index computation. Component-wise vec on the 68-byte stride explains the modest 9.38 GB/s; per-particle branches and spawn calls cap it far below ceiling.

## Verdict
Refuted — the algo never exceeds 9.38 GB/s = 31% of the 29.9 GB/s ceiling, even at the lowest death rate (q=0.01). The branch_flush bucket rises from 7.1% to 37.4% as death rate goes from 0.01 to 0.5, collapsing bandwidth to 5.0 GB/s (17% of ceiling). Per-particle component-wise vectorization cannot overcome the branchy respawn overhead; the hypothesis that it could approach the streaming ceiling does not hold at any measured death rate.
